muscle.definition: Authority or power or force (especially when used in a coercive way).

bicep.definition: People often say bicep for an upper-arm muscle or for both muscles together. Biceps brachii is the formal anatomy name.

tricep.definition: The large muscle at the back of the upper arm that helps straighten the elbow.
tricep.exampleUsage: The tricep contracts when the arm pushes something away.

quadricep.definition: One of the group of large muscles at the front of the thigh that help straighten the knee.
quadricep.exampleUsage: The quadriceps help support the knee when standing up.

hamstring.definition: To cripple by cutting the hamstring.

calf-muscle.definition: A muscle at the back of the lower leg that helps move the foot and ankle.
calf-muscle.exampleUsage: The calf muscle works when you rise onto your toes.

abdominal.definition: Of or relating to or near the abdomen.

deltoid.definition: A large triangular muscle covering the shoulder joint and serving to abduct and flex and extend and rotate the arm.

gluteus.definition: Any one of three large skeletal muscles that form the buttock and move the thigh.

pectoral.definition: Of or relating to the chest or thorax.

white-blood-cell.definition: A blood cell containing a nucleus that mainly protects the body from infection.
white-blood-cell.arabicTranslation: مصطلح طبي أو تشريحي يُسمّى «وهيتي بلوود كيلل»

antibody.definition: Any of a large variety of proteins normally present in the body or produced in response to an antigen which it neutralizes, thus producing an immune response.

antigen.definition: Any substance (as a toxin or enzyme) that stimulates an immune response in the body (especially the production of antibodies).

lymph-node.definition: A small immune organ produces lymph and lymphocytes, white blood cells carried through the lymphatic system.

tonsil.definition: Either of two masses of lymphatic tissue one on each side of the oral pharynx.

thymus.definition: Large genus of Old World mints: thyme.

bone-marrow.definition: Soft, blood-rich tissue inside bones makes blood cells and stores fat, especially in their spongy inner spaces.

immune-response.definition: A coordinated biological reaction in which the immune system detects and attacks harmful substances, disease-causing organisms, or abnormal cells.

vaccine.definition: Immunogen consisting of a suspension of weakened or dead pathogenic cells injected in order to stimulate the production of antibodies.

infection.definition: The communication of an attitude or emotional state among a number of people.

kidney.definition: Either of two bean-shaped excretory organs that filter wastes (especially urea) from the blood and excrete them and water in urine.

bladder.definition: A distensible membranous sac (usually containing liquid or gas).

ureter.definition: Either of a pair of thick-walled tubes that carry urine from the kidney to the urinary bladder.

urethra.definition: Duct through which urine is discharged in most mammals and which serves as the male genital duct.
urethra.exampleUsage: The urethra was identified during the lesson.

urine.definition: Liquid waste made by the kidneys and passed out of the body.

filtration.definition: The process whereby fluids pass through a filter or a filtering medium.

nephron.definition: Any of the small tubules that are the excretory units of the vertebrate kidney.

renal.definition: Of or relating to the kidneys.

toxin.definition: A poisonous substance produced during the metabolism and growth of certain microorganisms and some higher plant and animal species.
toxin.exampleUsage: The toxin was identified during the lesson.

hydration.definition: The process of combining with water.

cell-division.definition: The biological process in which one cell produces two new cells, typically through mitosis and cytokinesis.

dna.definition: (biochemistry) a long linear polymer found in the nucleus of a cell and formed from nucleotides and shaped like a double helix.

gene.definition: (genetics) a segment of DNA that is involved in producing a polypeptide chain.

chromosome.definition: A threadlike strand of DNA in the cell nucleus that carries the genes in a linear order.

embryo.definition: An animal organism in the early stages of growth and differentiation that in higher forms merge into fetal stages but in lower forms terminate in commencement of larval life.
embryo.exampleUsage: The embryo was identified during the lesson.

fetus.definition: An unborn or unhatched vertebrate in the later stages of development showing the main recognizable features of the mature animal.
fetus.exampleUsage: The fetus was identified during the lesson.

birth.definition: The time when something begins (especially life).

puberty.definition: The time of life when sex glands become functional.

skin-layer.definition: One of the distinct levels of tissue that make up the skin.
skin-layer.exampleUsage: The outer skin layer helps protect the body.

epidermis.definition: The outer layer of the skin covering the exterior body surface of vertebrates.

dermis.definition: The deep vascular inner layer of the skin.

hair-follicle.definition: A small tube-shaped cavity surrounds a hair root and connects with tiny muscles and sebaceous glands, which release oil.

sweat-gland.definition: A small organ in the skin that releases sweat, cooling the body and helping remove some waste while keeping the skin moist.

oil-gland.definition: A small organ produces and releases an oily substance.

melanin.definition: Insoluble pigments that account for the color of e.g. skin and scales and feathers.

keratin.definition: A fibrous scleroprotein that occurs in the outer layer of the skin and in horny tissues such as hair, feathers, nails, and hooves.

collagen.definition: A fibrous scleroprotein in bone and cartilage and tendon and other connective tissue.

pore.definition: Any small opening in the skin or outer surface of an animal.
pore.exampleUsage: The pore was identified during the lesson.
